Embroiderer
em-BROY-der-er
noun
From the Old French embrouder, “to ornament with needlework” (en-, “in,” + brouder, “to stitch,” of Frankish origin); hence one who works figures and colours into cloth with the needle.

Biblical Definition

An embroiderer works coloured thread into finished cloth with the needle — the “needlework” of the Authorized Version. He is one of the few craftsmen in Scripture whose skill is expressly traced to the Holy Ghost. For the tabernacle the LORD called Bezaleel by name (Exo 31:2) and said, “I have filled him with the spirit of God, in wisdom, and in understanding, and in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship” (Exo 31:3), and gave him Aholiab, who was “an engraver, and a cunning workman, and an embroiderer in blue, and in purple, and in scarlet, and fine linen” (Exo 38:23). Moses records the same of the whole company: “them hath he filled with wisdom of heart, to work all manner of work, of the engraver, and of the cunning workman, and of the embroiderer” (Exo 35:35). Two truths sit together here and neither may be let go. The first is that artistic skill is a gift of God, not a merely natural talent, and the embroiderer’s needle is as truly Spirit-given as the prophet’s tongue. The second is that this gift was never turned loose. Every colour, measure, and figure was commanded; the workmen wrought “according to all that the LORD had commanded” (Exo 36:1). Beauty in the worship of God is not optional and it is not free. It is prescribed.

Webster 1828 Definition

One who embroiders; a worker of figures and colours into cloth with the needle.

expand to see more

EMBROIDERER, one who embroiders; a worker of ornamental figures upon cloth with the needle.

From Old French embrouder, to ornament with needlework.

The Authorized Version usually calls the product needlework.

Aholiab of the tribe of Dan was an embroiderer in blue, purple, scarlet, and fine linen (Exo 38:23).

Their skill is expressly ascribed to the spirit of God (Exo 31:3; Exo 35:35).

Key Scripture

Exo 31:3 — "And I have filled him with the spirit of God, in wisdom, and in understanding, and in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship,"

Exo 36:1 — "Then wrought Bezaleel and Aholiab, and every wise hearted man, in whom the LORD put wisdom and understanding to know how to work all manner of work for the service of the sanctuary, according to all that the LORD had commanded."

Exo 35:32 — "And to devise curious works, to work in gold, and in silver, and in brass,"

Eze 27:16 — "Syria was thy merchant by reason of the multitude of the wares of thy making: they occupied in thy fairs with emeralds, purple, and broidered work, and fine linen, and coral, and agate."

Modern Corruption

Spirit-given artistry, held under the LORD's own pattern — the regulative principle applied to beauty.

expand to see more

Two corruptions meet at the embroiderer’s frame. The first is the bare and joyless instinct that treats beauty in the house of God as worldliness, as if the Lord who commanded blue, purple, scarlet, and fine twined linen were indifferent to loveliness. He is not. He named the artist, filled him with His Spirit, and specified the colours. The second corruption is the modern worship industry, which has taken the artist’s gift and cut it loose from the command — the service designed for effect, the lighting and staging tuned to produce a feeling, the platform run on the logic of performance. The tabernacle answers both. Its beauty was extravagant, and every thread of it was prescribed. Bezaleel had immense freedom of hand within an absolute boundary of command, and that is precisely what the regulative principle protects: not ugliness, but obedience.

There is a further word here about the ordinary Christian craftswoman and craftsman. Exodus 35 does not say the LORD filled Bezaleel with wisdom to preach; it says He filled him to work in gold, in blue, in purple, and with the needle. The Spirit’s gifting is not confined to the pulpit. A woman who sews well, a man who cuts a joint true, a hand that makes a plain thing beautiful — these are gifts of the same Giver, and they are to be offered back to Him with the same reverence. The world tells such workers that their skill is self-expression. Scripture tells them it is stewardship, given by God, to be used at His direction and for His glory.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

A worker of needlework; the Spirit-filled artisan of the tabernacle, free in hand and bound by command.

expand to see more

Embroiderer — Old French embrouder, to ornament with the needle.

The AV renders the product needlework and broidered work.

Bezaleel was called by name and filled with the spirit of God (Exo 31:2–3).

Aholiab of Dan was an embroiderer in blue, purple, scarlet, and fine linen (Exo 38:23).

All was wrought according to all that the LORD had commanded (Exo 36:1).

Usage

"The tabernacle’s embroiderer was Spirit-filled and pattern-bound at once."

"Beauty in worship is commanded, not invented."

"Skill in the hands is a gift of God and a stewardship, never mere self-expression."
